prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'Birth lowers resistance to pulmonary flow'. Two side-by-side tabletop wooden flow tracks viewed from above, clearly manufactured objects. Left heading 'Before transition': narrow gate across track, only a small teal arrow and a few teal round counters passing it, label 'Higher resistance'. Right heading 'After transition': the same gate wide open, a visibly broader teal arrow and more teal counters passing, label 'Lower resistance' and 'More pulmonary blood flow'. Above between models a separate small breath-swirl icon and O2 letter tile, labelled 'Aeration + oxygen rise', with a curved causal arrow pointing to right gate opening. Teal counters represent blood-flow units, never airway gas. No lungs, heart, arteries, vessels, baby or anatomical map. Bottom 'Gate analogy, not vascular anatomy'. No numbers, extra slogans or scenic decorations.

teaching.question: How do the first breaths affect pulmonary blood flow?
teaching.answer: Aeration and rising oxygen help dilate the pulmonary circulation, lowering pulmonary vascular resistance and allowing blood flow through the lungs to increase.

title: Birth lowers resistance to pulmonary flow
caption: Aeration and rising oxygen after birth help lower pulmonary vascular resistance, allowing pulmonary blood flow to increase. The gate illustrates resistance, not vascular anatomy.
alt: Two artificial flow channels compare a narrow gate with few blood-flow tokens before transition and an open gate with more tokens after aeration and oxygen rise.
